review_notes: I read the whole file and the downstream uses of `RootedCountingAmplification.bitCount` and `estimate` in CountingPublicWordBound.lean and ComputedCountingWords.lean. I also read the definition of `repetitionCount` in CommonBases.lean. The only simp-interface problem I found is the `bitCount_eq` lemma: it is stated in an unsuitable form, and the one downstream use that needs an unfolding bypasses it. I did not report `estimate`, which has no unfolding lemma, because I saw no downstream use that needs one. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour.

findings.excerpt: bitCount A s delta=64*(delta.den.bits.length+1)*RootedCountingWords.bitCount A s := rfl
findings.problem: This is the only unfolding equation for `bitCount`. It is stated after the main theorem and has no simp attribute. Its right-hand side hard-codes the body of `CommonBasesFPRAS.repetitionCount` (`64*(δ.den.bits.length+1)`) instead of keeping `repetitionCount delta`. It therefore does not match the definition `repetitionCount delta * RootedCountingWords.bitCount A s`, and a simp call using it would expand `repetitionCount` into raw arithmetic. The one downstream use that needs an unfolding, `amplified_public`, ignores the lemma. It runs `simp only [RootedCountingAmplification.bitCount, CommonBasesFPRAS.repetitionCount, ...]`, so it has to unfold both definitions by hand and then reassemble the product with `Nat.mul_le_mul hr hw`.
findings.proposed_change: Move the lemma next to `def bitCount`. State it at the definition's level of abstraction: `theorem bitCount_eq (A s delta) : bitCount A s delta = repetitionCount delta * RootedCountingWords.bitCount A s := rfl`. Mark it `@[simp]` if `bitCount` is meant to be unfolded automatically. Otherwise keep it as a plain `rw`/`simp only` lemma. If the expanded form is wanted, keep it as a separate lemma such as `bitCount_eq_expanded`. Then `amplified_public` can use `simp only [bitCount_eq, ...]`, or `rw [bitCount_eq]; exact Nat.mul_le_mul hr hw`, without unfolding `repetitionCount`.
findings.benefit: The normal form is stable and the intermediate `repetitionCount` abstraction is kept. Users of `bitCount` get one canonical rewrite rule in place of ad-hoc `simp only [bitCount, repetitionCount]` unfolding. Simp or rw no longer exposes the `64*(…bits.length+1)` implementation detail of `repetitionCount`, so downstream bounds like `repeats_le` that talk about `repetitionCount` still match syntactically.
